title: India Condemns Houthi Attack on Riyadh Tower, Confirms Two Indians Injured
excerpt: The MEA's November 25 statement called for an immediate cessation of attacks on Saudi civilian and energy infrastructure and said the Indian Embassy in Riyadh is assisting the two injured Indians and their families.
body:
• India's Ministry of External Affairs on Wednesday, November 25, strongly condemned the November 24 Houthi attack on a tower in Riyadh's financial district and called for an immediate cessation of such attacks.
  • Two Indian nationals were among the 11 people injured; the others were two Saudis, three Nepalese and four Egyptians, according to Saudi Civil Defence.
  • The Indian Embassy in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured Indians and their families — families seeking information should contact the embassy, which is coordinating help.
  • India reiterated its firm solidarity with Saudi Arabia and its support for the Kingdom's sovereignty and security.

India on Wednesday, November 25, strongly condemned the Houthi attack on a tower in Riyadh's financial district a day earlier, in which two Indian nationals were among 11 people injured, and called for an immediate halt to attacks on civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. The statement from the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) is New Delhi's formal response to the strike The Videshi reported on Tuesday.

"We strongly condemn the attack on one of the towers of the financial district in Riyadh on November 24 as well as the continued attacks targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia."

— Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India

"These attacks seriously endanger civilian lives, violate the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia, and undermine regional security and stability. We call for immediate cessation of such attacks," the ministry said. It confirmed that two Indians were among those injured and that the Embassy of India in Riyadh is providing all possible assistance to the injured and their families. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal posted the statement on X on November 25.

What happened on November 24

Saudi Arabia's General Directorate of Civil Defence said 11 people were injured when one of the towers of the Financial Centre in Riyadh was targeted on Tuesday, November 24, in what it described as a terrorist attack by Yemen's Houthi militia. The injured were two Saudi nationals, two Indians, three Nepalese nationals and four Egyptians. Emergency response teams reached the site immediately, and the spokesperson of the Saudi-led coalition called the strike a "cowardly terrorist attack" and said authorities were conducting an on-site investigation.

Solidarity with Riyadh

The MEA reiterated India's "firm solidarity with the people and Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia" and its "unwavering support to the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the security and safety of its citizens and residents," adding that India hopes peace and normalcy return to the region at the earliest.

The condemnation comes amid escalating tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthi authorities. Yemen's Houthi-controlled Ministry of Communications and Information Technology alleged on Monday that Saudi-led coalition aircraft had struck telecommunications buildings, workers' accommodation and a mosque in Al-Hudaydah Governorate, claiming 17 workers were killed and 11 injured in an initial toll — allegations the MEA statement did not address.

For the Indian community in Saudi Arabia — one of the largest expatriate populations in the Kingdom — the embassy remains the point of contact. The MEA has said the embassy is coordinating assistance to the two injured Indians and their families; no names or medical conditions of the injured have been released in the reports so far.
